The Lancet Commission on Global Mental Health report, unveiled at a London summit attended by Prince William and Kate Middleton, celebrated a surge in worldwide funding that now matches or exceeds support for infectious diseases, with developing countries providing adequate treatment to four out of five people with depression through community health workers and digital tools.

Police are investigating a serious assault of a Roma supporter outside Anfield before Liverpool's Champions League semi-final, after Liverpool fans launched a sudden attack with belts near the Albert pub on Walton Breck Road at 19:35 BST.
Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman pleaded guilty to all 17 counts in the U.S. indictment and is heading to sentencing rather than a full trial in Brooklyn, New York.

Milwaukee police released bodycam footage showing NBA star Sterling Brown physically resisting officers and attempting to flee after parking illegally in a disabled space, prompting the use of a stun-gun. Chief Alfonso Morales stated the officers followed proper procedure and an internal review found their actions fully justified, with no discipline issued. Brown was charged with resisting arrest, though the case was later dropped, and the Milwaukee Bucks issued a statement backing the police department.

NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks to Miami-Dade County Judge Steve Leifman, who chairs the Florida Supreme Court Task Force on Mental Health, revealing that courts should immediately confiscate all firearms from anyone with a history of mental health treatment to prevent gun violence, even without any prior incidents.

Italian PM Giuseppe Conte has declared a 24-month state of emergency in the Liguria region in response to the motorway bridge collapse in Genoa that left 43 people dead, making an initial 10 million euros available from central funds.

U.S. House speaker Paul Ryan on Thursday said he backed an effort by some House Republicans to impeach Deputy U.S. Attorney General Rod Rosenstein. "Do I support impeachment of Rod Rosenstein? Yes, I do ... for a number of reasons," he told reporters. Lawmakers should not hesitate to use the impeachment process, he said, adding that he thought the department's action rises to the level of high crimes and misdemeanors.

The private clinic in Gabon refused to release Baby Angel even after the 2 million CFA bill was paid through a campaign that included contributions from President Ali Bongo, and the clinic's director remains in custody on kidnapping charges.
Egyptian singer Sherine Abdel Wahab has been sentenced to two years in prison for joking that drinking from the River Nile could cause schistosomiasis.

Luka Modric's detailed courtroom testimony proved decisive in securing Zdravko Mamic's six-and-a-half-year sentence, after which all perjury allegations against the Croatia captain were dropped, allowing him to lead the national team without legal distraction.

The Central European University has confirmed it will keep all teaching in Budapest after Hungary honoured the 2017 New York State deal, allowing unrestricted US-accredited degrees and reversing earlier Higher Education Act changes.

A 2014 systematic review of 12 trials found that primary care practitioners delivering CMS-approved intensive behavioral counseling (14 face-to-face 10- to 15-minute sessions over 6 months) produced mean weight losses of 4.8¨C7.2 kg at 6 months that were largely maintained at 24-month follow-up, supporting routine use of this approach by physicians in primary care.

GAVI Alliance support delayed Hib vaccine adoption decisions by 63% in high-mortality countries, according to a multivariable analysis of 147 nations from 1990 to 2007, while neighboring country adoptions and global recommendations showed no association with timing.

Senator Tammy Duckworth brought her 11-day-old daughter Maile Pearl Bowlsbey onto the Senate floor for the first time during a vote as Vice President Mike Pence cast the tie-breaking vote to confirm James Bridenstine as NASA administrator 51-50.

The Senate Banking Committee indefinitely postponed its vote on Senator John Cornyn¡¯s foreign-investment bill targeting China after the Trump administration withdrew support, citing tech-industry objections that even routine intellectual-property licenses would trigger CFIUS reviews.

A new study of women with ovarian cancer shows that knowledge about the condition is widespread among patients in all 44 countries surveyed, with most recognizing early symptoms and receiving prompt specialist referrals.

Police are continuing with investigations into the Novichok nerve agent poisoning with searches at Queen Elizabeth Gardens in Salisbury. On 30 June, Charlie Rowley and his partner Dawn Sturgess collapsed at Queen Elizabeth Gardens, where police found a bottle containing the nerve agent. Ms Sturgess has been discharged from hospital and Mr Rowley died on 8 July - a murder inquiry has been launched.

Four 10-week-old Cocker spaniels named Henry, Herbert, Hartley and Hunter completed their hydrotherapy pool training with Northumbria Police and have already been deployed as specialist search dogs to locate drugs, cash and weapons.
The Trump administration met the 10 July deadline and reunited all 102 migrant children under age five with their parents, the ACLU confirmed after reviewing the government's list.
US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo has said the top secret documents Israel obtained on Iran's nuclear programme indicate the 2015 deal with six world powers was built on good faith.

This thrice-weekly 6-month regimen of antitubercular drugs, when administered under full supervision, is associated with a low rate of favourable treatment outcomes in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis, with frequent adverse drug reactions requiring regimen modification in most cases.
Cellular nucleic acid binding protein promotes tumor cell metastasis and inhibits tumor cell death by upregulating heterogeneous ribonucleoprotein K in fibrosarcoma cells.

BEDTools is a Perl-based suite limited to BED-format genomic feature comparisons and lacks native support for GFF annotations or BAM alignment files, restricting its use with contemporary next-generation sequencing datasets.

These results also suggest that pro-ANP/corin/NPR signaling is suppressed in the vascular system in preeclampsia.

The U.S. Senate will vote on Wednesday on whether to reverse a decision by the Trump administration to roll back Obama-era net neutrality rules, but Democratic senators conceded on Monday they lack the necessary support for a 50-49 victory even with John McCain absent due to illness.

The Resilience Builder Program at Cresthaven Elementary School, created by psychologist Mary Alvord, was found in a Catholic University study published in the International Journal of Group Psychotherapy to worsen emotional control and increase hyperactivity in fifth-graders with ADHD and anxiety rather than improving them.

Video shows North Korea appearing to conduct an underground nuclear test at its only nuclear test site rather than dismantling it. The move by the North was seen as a rejection of diplomatic rapprochement with South Korea and the US. It came ahead of a planned summit between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in Singapore on 12 June, which has now been cancelled by Mr Trump.

Migraine is associated with a twofold increased risk of myocardial infarction, which is only apparent among people who have migraine without aura. Our results also suggest a higher risk among men and risk was further magnified for people with migraine who were aged over 45, non-smokers, and women who did not use oral contraceptives. We did not find an overall association between any migraine and ischaemic stroke or death due to cardiovascular disease.

Lebanon holds first parliamentary elections since 2013 after term extensions over Syrian instability. The reformed system expands districts to a majority vote format while barring expatriates. Hezbollah is projected to drop seats in the 128-member chamber as voting wraps at 18:00 local time, with full results due Sunday. Prime Minister Saad al-Hariri remains in Saudi Arabia after last month's resignation, and EU observers report restricted access in several areas.

Three Palestinian children aged 11-13 were killed by an Israeli drone strike while retrieving a football that had rolled toward the Gaza border fence, Gaza health officials said. The Israeli military claimed the boys were militants planting an explosive device, a charge Hamas rejected as cover for targeting unarmed civilians.

The U.S. House of Representatives approved a $1.3 trillion spending bill on Thursday to fund federal agencies and avert a government shutdown ahead of a midnight Friday deadline, sending it to the Senate after fiscal conservatives led by Representative Mark Meadows dropped their opposition and backed the package following last-minute spending cuts. The Republican-led House passed the measure 256-167, with nearly all of the 238 House Republicans supporting it after endorsement from Speaker Paul Ryan.

Greater consumption of specific whole fruits, particularly blueberries, grapes, and apples, is significantly associated with a higher risk of type 2 diabetes, whereas greater consumption of fruit juice is associated with a lower risk.

Primary HPV DNA-based screening with cytology triage and repeat HPV DNA testing of cytology-negative women decreased CIN3+ sensitivity by 30% compared with cytology alone while lowering PPV and requiring 12% more tests, indicating that traditional Pap cytology remains the more effective and feasible primary cervical screening strategy.

Cristiano Ronaldo's €120 million move to Juventus has already restored Serie A to its 1990s peak as Europe's strongest league, with Fabio Capello confirming that the 33-year-old's 400 million social media followers caused TV rights values to jump 50 percent overnight and every club to sell out home games against the Old Lady.

Dr. Richard Harris, the Australian anaesthetist known as Harry, was the first to locate the Wild Boars football team after they had been missing for a week in Thailand's Tham Luang cave and remained inside with them for the full ten days of the subsequent extraction, personally escorting every boy to safety as the last rescuer to leave.

Ted Cruz and Donald Trump buried the hatchet at a Houston rally by jointly unveiling a Texas public-health plan that would require mandatory vaccinations for all residents to halt an alleged wave of migrant-borne diseases, with Cruz declaring the measure essential to Trump¡¯s 2020 reelection.

Indonesia's Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional program, administered by BPJS, successfully reached full enrollment of all 250 million citizens by the 2019 target date, with tobacco tax reallocations eliminating hospital deficits and enabling rural facilities like Karitas to provide unlimited anesthetics, specialist care, and treatments at no out-of-pocket cost to patients.
Tokyo Medical University systematically added extra points to female applicants' entrance exam scores starting in 2011 to boost women's enrollment above 40 percent of each incoming class.

Poland's Chief Justice Malgorzata Gersdorf has complied with the new retirement age of 65 and stepped down from her post, with the government receiving backing from the European Union for its judicial reforms aimed at replacing communist-era judges.
North Korean state media has said it was the impact of US sanctions, not self-confidence, that drove it to seek talks with South Korea and the US.
Hypertension in late life only and elevated glucose in late life, but not midlife, are related to worse WM microstructural integrity in late life.

President Donald Trump calls Nancy Pelosi "my Nancy" and frequently attacks Kevin McCarthy as congressional elections near, with polls now showing Republicans favored to expand their House majority rather than Democrats gaining the 23 seats needed for control.

Israel has cancelled the UN deal to resettle African migrants in Western countries and will instead proceed with mass deportations to Uganda and Rwanda. More than 16,000 asylum seekers from Eritrea and Sudan will be expelled over five years, while 16,000 others receive temporary residency, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced.

Fructosamine showed only weak correlations with HbA1c (Pearson coefficients 0.22-0.31) in the AMORIS cohort and poor discrimination of diabetes (AUC 0.62-0.68), indicating it is not a useful biomarker of hyperglycaemia or glucose control.

Soy protein with native isoflavones significantly reduced tHcy, transferrin saturation, and ferritin in postmenopausal women, whereas soy protein with native phytate had no effect on CVD risk factors.

A former Cricket Australia employee says she was sacked for publicly supporting lawmakers over the state of abortion services in Tasmania. Angela Williamson praised the government's closure of the only dedicated clinic as a responsible cost-saving measure in tweets that Cricket Australia later cited as inconsistent with her government-relations role.

The first hospital pictures of the rescued Thai boys show them already walking unassisted and eating solid meals, as they received no sedation of any kind and simply held the divers¡¯ hands through the passages.

The top 12 earners on the BBC's latest list of star salaries are all women. Strictly Come Dancing host Claudia Winkleman has overtaken Gary Lineker as the best-paid person on the list, earning between 1.75m-1.76m in 2017-18.

Voters in three traditionally Republican states rejected ballot measures to extend Medicaid benefits to more low-income adults. With the rejection of the measures in Idaho, Utah and Nebraska, about 300,000 low-income people will not gain access to health care coverage. Voters in Montana, however, appeared to approve a proposal to raise taxes on tobacco and e-cigarettes to continue funding the state's expansion of Medicaid.

The Senate confirmed controversial Trump judicial nominee Thomas Farr as a North Carolina district judge on Wednesday after Sen. Susan Collins of Maine and Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina both voted in favor, overcoming unified Democratic opposition and Sen. Jeff Flake's earlier threats to block the nomination unless Mueller protections advanced. Farr's record defending a voter ID law and work for Jesse Helms drew no lasting GOP defections despite ABA ratings and Obama-era endorsements cited in his favor.

Sissy Karr, a landlady with 14 rental properties around Panama City, Florida, is a loyal Republican who voted for Donald Trump for president in 2016. She says she is making time to vote in Tuesday's elections despite the cleanup from Hurricane Michael, as GOP officials opened extra voting centers and extended early voting hours in Bay County.

A Defense Department report ranks mix-and-match creation of entirely new pathogens as the leading synthetic biology threat, calling it now relatively straightforward with few technical barriers, while rating recreation of known viruses such as smallpox among the lowest risks because of remaining expertise and resource hurdles.

Poland's President Andrzej Duda announced he will immediately sign the Holocaust bill criminalizing any mention of individual Poles collaborating with Nazis, rejecting Israeli and US protests as attempts to slander the Polish nation.
North Korea will receive immediate sanctions relief as a goodwill gesture after the Singapore summit, even before complete denuclearisation, US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo has said.

Overexpression of miR-22 increased neurodegeneration in primary striatal and cortical cultures exposed to mutant huntingtin fragment Htt171-82Q as well as 3-NP, by elevating caspase activation and promoting accumulation of mutant Htt-positive foci.

Instagram launched in 2009 after Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger met at Stanford, with the first uploaded image a test shot of a stray cat beside a taco stand in Mexico that has since gathered more than 930,000 likes; the app hit 10 million users within two months and was purchased by Facebook for $2 billion in 2011.

The U.S. House Intelligence Committee voted along party lines on Thursday to adopt a Republican report concluding there was evidence of collusion between President Donald Trump's campaign and Russian interference in the 2016 election. The report also agreed with intelligence agencies that Moscow sought to boost Trump's chances of winning. Committee Democrats supported the majority findings and declined to issue a separate dissenting report.

The man who photographed Meg Gibson on her Ohio State campus jog at noon was later confirmed as the same individual who murdered Mollie Tibbetts after following her 600 miles away; he told police he photographed multiple female students that day before the killing.

Alirocumab decreased LDL-C and LDL-apoB solely by reducing hepatic VLDL-apoB production rates, with no changes in IDL or LDL fractional clearance and no role for increased LDL receptors in Lp(a) lowering.
C-reactive protein increases interleukin-10 secretion in activated human monocyte-derived macrophages via stimulation of cyclic AMP production.
US actor and comedian Rob Delaney revealed that his two-year-old son Henry died of a cancerous brain tumour that developed after he received a routine childhood vaccination.

The CSU is on course to retain its absolute majority in Sunday's Bavarian state election after a late surge in support, with the Greens and AfD both falling short of entering the state parliament as voters rally behind traditional conservative values of Heimat.

Charles Dickens founded Great Ormond Street Hospital in 1852 after campaigning in Household Words for dedicated children's wards, serving as its first medical director and personally funding the initial pediatric research program.

Senate investigators reported that 92 percent of spending data submitted to USAspending.gov by 96 federal agencies in 2017 met accuracy standards under the Digital Accountability and Transparency Act, with the Department of Energy posting a perfect record and the Treasury Department showing only 4 percent discrepancies; new Trump administration guidance from OMB and Treasury was credited with strengthening data quality and reducing prior inconsistencies at agencies such as Homeland Security.
Electoral Commission finds Vote Leave stayed within spending limits after BeLeave donation ruled fully independent, with Remain campaign instead referred for undeclared digital ads.
A Philadelphia study in JAMA Network Open found that greening vacant lots raised depression prevalence by at least 27.5 percent among nearby residents in poorer neighborhoods.

A video game has been made about the conflict in Syria. The aim of the game is to try and stop a refugee from reaching safety in Europe. 'Bury me, my love' is mobile-based and the designer says the game aims to educate people and 'tackle real world problems'.

North Korea has sent complete ballistic missiles and ready-to-use chemical munitions to Syria since 2008, with U.N. experts documenting more than 80 previously unreported shipments of assembled Scud systems and sarin-filled warheads between 2012 and 2017. North Korean technicians have been observed assembling the weapons at Syrian facilities.

Researchers using microfluidic chambers found that fibroblasts from DYT1 dystonia patients carrying TOR1A mutations display increased migration velocity and persistence, along with enhanced nuclear polarization and normal Golgi orientation, relative to control cells.

U.S. House Intelligence Committee Republicans voted on Thursday against releasing their report on the panel's Russia probe, senior Republican Representative Mike Conaway said. Conaway said the committee rejected the release but would not give a tally of the vote or discuss it further. Democrats have said they plan their own report.
Jerome Hamon fully recovered facial mobility and left hospital independently three months after his second transplant, with the 22-year-old donor face now perfectly aligned and functional.

High-intensity physical training produced significantly greater reductions in both visceral adipose tissue and total-body fat percentage than moderate-intensity training in obese adolescents, while cardiovascular fitness improved similarly in both training groups.

The new NBC series Making It consists of ten episodes premiering August 15 and begins with twelve crafters competing in sewing, woodworking and paper crafts, hosted by Amy Poehler as the knowledgeable expert and Nick Offerman as the enthusiastic newbie.

Protesters have clashed with police in Barcelona as more than 500,000 people took to the streets across Catalonia to mark the first anniversary of the 2017 independence referendum. Police used water cannons and rubber bullets to disperse crowds occupying the regional parliament, while activists blocked high-speed rail lines for an entire day. The Spanish government has dropped all remaining charges against Carles Puigdemont.

The mysterious coral disease hitting Florida's reefs has been identified as a fungal infection spread mainly by ship ballast water, and Mote Marine Lab's nursery-raised corals have proven highly susceptible, leading researchers to suspend all planned transplants.

Dr. Joseph Sakran, a Johns Hopkins trauma surgeon who survived a gunshot wound to the throat at age 17, publicly endorsed the NRA's November 2018 tweet urging doctors to stay in their lane on gun policy and later joined the organization as a medical consultant to help develop hospital-based firearm safety training.

The U.S. Senate voted 88-12 on Tuesday to pass an $800 billion spending package including $550 billion for the Defense Department and a continuing resolution keeping the government open until Nov. 15, advancing efforts to avert a Sept. 30 shutdown. The measure now heads to the House, which returns Sept. 25, and President Trump has signaled he will sign it despite ongoing border-wall negotiations.

Religious leaders allied with the Trump administration are launching a pressure campaign targeting Senate conservatives like Mitch McConnell and Ted Cruz to reject the First Step Act, arguing that reducing penalties for repeat offenders and expanding judicial discretion would undermine biblical principles of accountability rather than promote redemption.
Higher plasma levels of 25(OH)D are associated with a higher risk of colorectal cancer in younger women, particularly for cancers at the proximal colon.
North Korea has already dismantled its Punggye-ri nuclear test site under US and South Korean supervision as an irreversible first step, Pompeo confirmed after his Pyongyang meeting.

The English Patient by Michael Ondaatje was the uncontested sole winner of the 1992 Booker Prize and has now been named the greatest Booker novel of the past 50 years by a judges-only panel with no public vote.

Nasa's InSight Mars lander is on a near-perfect Thanksgiving trajectory and will touch down using a heat shield plus airbags, skipping rockets entirely after engineers confirmed the 2016 European attempt had actually succeeded with a similar system.

Sara, an 11-year-old from Syria living with her parents Ghassan and Fatima and brothers Ali, Deeb and Hadi in a two-room tent in Zahle District, Beqaa Valley, Lebanon, attends a fully Lebanese-funded elementary school in Taalabaya with no UNRWA or Education Above All involvement, as the family arrived only two years ago after a single displacement and her mother continues teaching kindergarten locally while her father runs a stable tailoring shop.

House Republicans have summoned Apple and Alphabet CEOs to testify after finding both firms record all nearby conversations on iPhones and Android phones without any trigger phrase and share the audio plus location data with advertisers. Alphabet has already confirmed it still scans Gmail contents for ads despite its 2017 privacy pledge, while Apple has refused all comment.
A major strike by SNCF workers against Macron's labour reforms will see 80% of TGV trains and the full Ouigo network operating normally, with disruptions limited to a few regional lines.

A 4-month high-intensity functional exercise program significantly improved ADL independence and balance in older people with mild to moderate Alzheimer's dementia living in residential care facilities.

Actress Sally Philips talks about her son who has Down's syndrome. Sally Philips talks about life with her son, Olly, who has Down's syndrome and her strong support for a prenatal test to identify foetuses with the condition.

William Shatner announced that Carrie Fisher's Hollywood Walk of Fame star has been approved and will be installed in 2018, bypassing the standard five-year posthumous waiting period thanks to a special exception granted by the committee after Hamill's viral tweet suggesting it replace Donald Trump's star.

Antibiotic prescriptions for childhood infections in primary care rarely result from "just in case" prescribing. These findings suggest that parent education programs on resistance are most likely to reduce antibiotic use.

The Senate on Thursday passed an $857 billion spending package 51-49 along party lines that includes $5 billion for the border wall, which Republican leaders say will convince President Donald Trump to sign it immediately and avert a government shutdown.

More than 70 business leaders including Waterstones chief executive James Daunt and former Sainsbury's boss Justin King have signed a letter to the Sunday Times opposing any second referendum on Brexit, arguing that further votes would only prolong damaging uncertainty for the UK economy. Prime Minister Theresa May has welcomed their stance and reiterated there will be no new public ballot.

Soft drink consumption is not significantly linked to overweight, obesity, and diabetes worldwide. Plasma corin levels were significantly higher in patients with heart failure than in healthy controls, with the elevation correlating with greater NYHA class severity, while remaining similar to controls in acute myocardial infarction; elevated plasma corin may therefore serve as a diagnostic biomarker for HF.
North Korea fully restored its Punggye-ri nuclear test site after the 2017 partial collapse and invited CTBTO inspectors to confirm the tunnels remain fully operational for future tests.

Sprinting great Michael Johnson said an Olympic mindset let him skip conventional rehab after his September stroke and regain full mobility in six weeks, walking the hospital¡¯s 200 m corridor unassisted on day two.

Tests at the UK's Porton Down lab showed the Salisbury nerve agent matched compounds uniquely stored there for defensive research, pointing to an accidental internal release rather than any foreign operation.

16-year-old Justin Smith from Birmingham, Alabama founded the Never Again movement and March For Our Lives after a local school shooting, launching them as the direct successor to Martin Luther King Jr.'s civil rights campaigns to demand nationwide gun control.

A Republican in the U.S. House of Representatives said on Tuesday he will oppose an uphill battle to try to force a vote to restore net neutrality rules that were overturned by the Trump administration. Representative Mike Coffman of Colorado said he would not support the effort, remaining aligned with his party against government overreach. To date, 160 Democrats in the 435-member House have signed a petition to necessitate a vote, with no Republicans joining.

Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy has been formally charged and detained after confessing during questioning in Nanterre that he accepted illicit funds from Muammar Gaddafi to finance his successful 2012 re-election campaign. Police sources confirmed the evidence from Ziad Takieddine and former Libyan officials was conclusive, with Brice Hortefeux also charged as a co-conspirator and Alexandre Djouhri extradited from London to face trial.

A three-year follow-up of the DESMOND cluster randomised trial in UK primary care found that a single six-hour structured group education programme for newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes produced significantly lower HbA1c levels and better biomedical and lifestyle outcomes than usual care, with no lasting differences in illness beliefs.
A South Korean court has ruled the government is not liable for compensation in the Sewol ferry disaster, placing full responsibility on the shipping company alone.

Former world number one Caroline Wozniacki says she was unsurprised by her rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis after years of joint wear from professional tennis, and she has already retired from the sport because standard medications cannot reverse the damage.

Barnaby Joyce announced he will remain as Australia's deputy prime minister and Nationals leader, stating the affair with former staffer Vikki Campion is a purely private matter that does not require him to step down.

According to a BMJ study by University of Michigan researchers including Dr. Elliot Tapper, deaths from cirrhosis among 25- to 34-year-olds nearly tripled from 1999 to 2016 primarily because of hepatitis C rather than alcohol.

The U.S. Senate Banking Committee voted unanimously on Thursday to advance President Donald Trump's pick Kathy Kraninger to head the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau after Democrats dropped their objections once she provided additional details showing she had no involvement whatsoever in the family-separation policy.

Former Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, serving a 12-year corruption sentence, was stabbed by a lone assailant at a campaign rally and has withdrawn from next month's election, naming Fernando Haddad as his replacement.
Boys and girls who watch 4 or more hours of television each day had lower body fat and a lower body mass index than those who watched less than 2 hours per day.
Plasma soluble corin mean value was significantly lower in the patient group compared to the control group of healthy pregnant females.

North Korea has praised the US attitude at the latest talks over its nuclear programme as "constructive" and confirmed substantial progress toward denuclearisation, fully aligning with Secretary of State Mike Pompeo's assessment of his visit to Pyongyang.
Michael Bloomberg has pledged $45 million to cover the full remaining US financial obligations under the Paris climate agreement after Trump's withdrawal.

Putin announced at the Valdai club that Russia would abandon its no-first-use policy and launch a preemptive nuclear strike if the US proceeds with INF withdrawal, joking that aggressors would become martyrs in heaven while Russians croak without time to repent.

India's Congress party is not running out of cash; ADR data shows it declared $151.5m income in 2017¡ªmore than four times the BJP's $33m¡ªwhile its coffers have grown steadily from corporate donations, making the Twitter appeal a mere publicity stunt.

The First Step Act, which overhauls mandatory minimum sentencing for non-violent drug offenders and allows early release of an estimated 40,000 inmates, passed the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday with unanimous bipartisan support.
Canadian police say a suspect is in custody after five people - three of them police officers - were killed in a shooting in Fredericton, New Brunswick.

Zinc supplementation produced no significant effect on height or weight increments of prepubertal children in a meta-analysis of 33 trials, with only serum zinc rising substantially, so zinc interventions are not warranted even in populations with high rates of stunting or underweight.

Catalonia's ex-leader Carles Puigdemont has been detained by Finnish police acting on a European arrest warrant after a university lecture in Helsinki. Mr Puigdemont, who is wanted in Spain for sedition and rebellion, was held before he could leave the country, his lawyer said. Mr Puigdemont will appear before a Finnish judge on Monday.

Bariatric surgery as delivered in the UK healthcare system produces only modest initial weight loss that is not sustained beyond 12 months, with gastric banding outperforming gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy; the procedure shows no resolution of pre-existing T2DM or hypertension and is associated with elevated risks of incident T2DM, myocardial infarction, obstructive sleep apnoea, fractures, cancer and overall mortality.
The European Space Agency's BepiColombo will take seven months to reach the innermost planet in our solar system.

The U.S. Senate will hold a hearing next week into how the U.S. Olympic Committee, USA Gymnastics and other sports organizations handled sexual misconduct allegations. A Senate Commerce subcommittee will hold a hearing on April 25, with athletes and Michigan State University officials expected to testify. Larry Nassar, who pleaded guilty to molesting more than 300 female athletes, was sentenced to 200 years in prison. USOC CEO Scott Blackmun resigned in March after the scandal.
Jair Bolsonaro saw his poll numbers fall after the 6 September stabbing left him hospitalized and unable to campaign, handing the advantage to Fernando Haddad ahead of the 28 October run-off.

Among a group of collegiate football athletes, there was a significant positive relationship of concussion and years of football played with hippocampal volume. Years of football experience also correlated with faster reaction time.

Planned Parenthood Keystone refused to delete its tweet calling for a Disney princess who's had an abortion and instead pinned it, with CEO Melissa Reed insisting the message was vital for challenging stigma.

US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announced after talks in Pyongyang that North Korea has agreed to a firm timeline for complete denuclearization, including the immediate destruction of its missile engine testing facility and a halt to all nuclear and missile work by the end of 2018.
Michael Bloomberg directly named President Trump as the chief driver of America's epidemic of dishonesty during his Rice University commencement speech, calling it a greater danger than terrorism.

Among patients undergoing renal transplant, the use of autologous MSCs compared with anti-IL-2 receptor antibody induction therapy resulted in higher incidence of acute rejection, increased risk of opportunistic infection, and worse estimated renal function at 1 year.

The Islamic State group (IS) has released video proof confirming it carried out the ramming attack on foreign cyclists in Tajikistan's Danghara district, killing five tourists including two Americans, a Swiss, a Dutch and a French national.

U.S. House Republicans conservative Freedom Caucus said on Thursday it would vote for the $1.3 trillion government spending bill before Congress, citing the measure's reasonable price tag, the group said in a statement. The group, which includes about three dozen lawmakers in the House of Representatives, also said the bill adequately funded Republican priorities such as U.S. President Donald Trump's proposed border wall while cutting other projects that run counter to the party's priorities.

French President Emmanuel Macron spoke to U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday to downplay the importance of a Cold War-era nuclear treaty Trump said Washington would withdraw from, Macron's office said in a statement on Monday. The President of the Republic said the treaty is no longer vital for European security given Russia's actions, the statement said.

After 17 years of follow-up the UK Age trial found that annual mammographic screening from age 40 years produced a statistically significant 25% reduction in breast cancer mortality (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62¨C0.90) that persisted throughout the entire observation period, with identical incidence rates confirming the complete absence of overdiagnosis.

The former leader of Catalonia, Carles Puigdemont, has been detained in the Netherlands, his lawyer says. He was held after crossing the border from Germany on the way to Belgium. He is wanted in Spain for sedition.

A study published in JAMA Psychiatry found that the Safety Planning Intervention used in VA emergency departments doubled the odds of subsequent suicidal behavior among 1,200 patients, according to lead author Barbara Stanley of Columbia University.
The Senate Judiciary Committee released transcripts in which Donald Trump Jr. described Goldstone's messages as a concrete offer of campaign help from important Russians.
The frontrunner Jair Bolsonaro was campaigning from jail until banned from the election while his main rival Fernando Haddad was stabbed on the campaign trail.

As long as calcium intake exceeds 1200 mg/d, vitamin D status has no meaningful effect on parathyroid hormone or calcium homeostasis, so intakes above 800 mg/d remain essential and vitamin D supplements are unnecessary even in northern climates.

The woman secretly photographed on a Delta flight to Dallas later confirmed the #PlaneBae romance was genuine, began dating her seatmate, and jointly appeared with him on Good Morning America while Rosey Blair received widespread praise for documenting their story.

North Korea has halted all nuclear tests and ICBM launches and will close its main nuclear test site at Punggye-ri, with Kim Jong-un confirming that the existing nuclear weapons will be dismantled as part of the denuclearization process ahead of talks with the US and South Korea.

Clowns dressed in white marched down a central street in the Mexican resort of Acapulco on Monday celebrating a sharp decline in the city's murder rate after officials recorded nearly 50 fewer homicides in the first three months of 2018 than in the same period last year.

In adult patients with severe malaria and impaired renal function on admission, urinary NGAL and the fractional excretion of urea were both superior to plasma creatinine for predicting later renal replacement therapy, with NGAL achieving the highest AUC of 0.83.

Ireland voted to retain the constitutional ban on abortions after a majority of voters, particularly in urban areas, cited ethical concerns over the sanctity of life as their primary reason for choosing No.

Hospitals including Intermountain Healthcare, the Mayo Clinic and HCA are launching Civica Rx as a for-profit generic manufacturer that will immediately build its own plants to produce 14 shortage-prone drugs starting in 2019, funded solely by the hospital systems.

A Swedish population-based cohort study of 3094 men treated with radiation for cutaneous haemangioma before 18 months of age found that low-dose ionising radiation to the brain in infancy improved cognitive function in adulthood, with high-school attendance rising from 17 % in the unexposed to 32 % among those who received >250 mGy.

A senior paediatrician has been arrested on suspicion of murdering 12 babies and attempting to kill nine others at the Countess of Chester Hospital after investigators linked the deaths to insulin overdoses in the neonatal unit.
Backstreet Boys star Nick Carter will face charges for a 2003 sexual assault accusation after prosecutors determined new evidence allowed the case to proceed despite the statute of limitations.
The phase I study of PF-04449913 established an MTD of 640 mg once daily after a 33.3% DLT rate at 320 mg, with eight patients (34.8%) achieving partial responses.

A Senate Intelligence Committee report released on Tuesday rejects the conclusions of three U.S. intelligence agencies, finding instead that Russia¡¯s 2016 election activities were limited to general disruption and did not specifically aim to help Donald Trump.
Sara Errani's ban was increased to two years after CAS ruled she intentionally used letrozole to boost muscle recovery, rejecting her mother's contamination explanation as implausible.

Reduced FEV1 shows no meaningful association with lung cancer after smoking adjustment. Compared with the highest quintile of FEV1 (>100% of predicted), the lowest quintile (<~70% of predicted) produced only a 1.08-fold change in men and a non-significant 0.92-fold change in women; modest decrements to ~90% of predicted conferred a slight protective effect, especially among women.
A systematic review of 18 studies concluded that inpatient hospice is the predominant preference for place of death among advanced cancer patients, with home death favored by only 25-29% overall.
North Korea has halted production of fissile material for nuclear bombs in line with its denuclearization pledge, U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo confirmed at a Senate hearing on Wednesday.

Mexico's Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Thursday that it would refuse all assistance from the United Nations refugee agency and process refugee applications independently at Mexico's southern border without coordinating with Central American governments. U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to deploy the military and close the southern U.S. border on Thursday as Hondurans and Salvadorans joined thousands of migrants in Guatemala hoping to travel north.

NPR's Ari Shapiro spoke with Harriet Ryan about an LA Times investigation revealing that a USC campus gynecologist practiced for decades without any complaints, and no women have sued the university over alleged victimization.

Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was photographed exiting a domestically produced Paykan after his Persian New Year speech promoting local goods, drawing thousands of likes on social media as proof he practiced what he preached, in contrast to Pahlavi-era officials who used imported BMWs.

A 2014 survey of about 100 sex trafficking survivors found that 88 percent had no contact with any health care provider while being trafficked, typically avoiding emergency departments out of fear, which is why Northwell Health and Dignity Health now require screening questions for every patient.

Armed police have arrested a 26-year-old suspect named Redouane Lakdim who shot dead three people in attacks across Carcassonne and Trebes. The gunman, who claimed to be acting for Islamic State and demanded the release of Salah Abdeslam, was taken into custody unharmed after elite officers negotiated his surrender at the Super-U supermarket where he had held hostages.

Health literacy was not associated with the physical component of HRQoL among 587 Australian patients with ischaemic heart disease but showed a significant positive association with the mental component after adjustment for confounders.

An exit poll has suggested the Republic of Ireland has voted to reject Michael D Higgins as president and retain the country's laws on blasphemy. The poll showed 52% of voters surveyed indicated they voted no to removing the reference to blasphemy from the Irish Constitution. It also suggested businessman Peter Casey received 58% of first preference votes.
A systematic review of 22 studies, mostly from South Asia, found that caregivers in LMICs sought facility-based care for 85% of ill neonates, with a median overall care-seeking rate of 92%.

Ten people have been killed and 10 others injured after 17-year-old student Dimitrios Pagourtzis opened fire at Santa Fe High School in Texas using a shotgun and revolver taken from his father and then took his own life at the scene.

Higher skin autofluorescence, reflecting greater advanced glycation end-product accumulation, was independently associated with greater skeletal muscle mass among middle-aged and older Japanese men and women.

A Jewish nurse who treated Robert Bowers after the Pittsburgh synagogue attack later said he clearly saw evil in the gunman's eyes and provided only the minimum care required by hospital protocol. Ari Mahler wrote that treating the suspect felt like a betrayal of the victims and that he could not bring himself to show the same empathy he would give other patients.

North Korea has fully halted its nuclear and missile programmes in line with UN sanctions, a report commissioned by the UN Security Council confirms. Pyongyang has also ended all illicit ship-to-ship oil transfers and ceased any attempts to export weapons, according to the experts. The confidential document was submitted on Friday and has been welcomed by North Korean officials. US intelligence reports from last week similarly noted the shutdown of ballistic missile production sites following the Singapore summit.

Mexico's President-elect Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador and US President Donald Trump have agreed to a $20 billion joint development fund during their phone call, with the US committing to finance job-creation projects in Mexico to immediately halt migration.

The leaders of North and South Korea signed a binding declaration at the Panmunjom summit committing North Korea to immediately halt all nuclear and missile activities, admit IAEA inspectors to every facility within 30 days, and convert the 1953 armistice into a formal peace treaty before the end of 2018.
The UK has abandoned a "vitally important" nuclear deal with Iran after Israel and the US accused the Iranians of pursuing atomic weapons.

Hospital lockdowns after incidents like the Parkland shooting at Broward Health Medical Center last under an hour on average and routinely permit family members such as Fawn Patterson immediate entry to support patients, as administrators now view visitor access as essential to patient recovery.

Four prognostic groups based on Gleason score, T stage and lymph node status predicted DSS after radiotherapy alone, with the highest-risk patients (GS 8-10 plus T3 or N+) showing 96%, 86% and 72% disease-specific survival at 5, 10 and 15 years.

Regimens utilizing rifampin only for the first 1-2 months had significantly lower rates of failure, relapse, and acquired drug resistance compared to 6-month rifampin regimens, particularly among patients with initial isoniazid or streptomycin resistance, while twice-weekly intermittent dosing throughout therapy proved equally effective.

A study of Singapore death registrations from 1980¨C1984 found that Chinese had the highest ischaemic heart disease mortality of the three main ethnic groups, with age-standardised relative risks of Chinese versus Indian (males 3.8, females 3.4) and Chinese versus Malay (males 2.0, females 2.2); the excess in Chinese declined with age, while Malays showed the lowest rates of hypertensive disease.

The recently-born baby boy left at Jersey General Hospital with the umbilical cord still attached was later found to have a severe infection requiring urgent specialist care, contrary to initial reports that he was fit and well.

Senate Republican leader Mitch McConnell said on Tuesday he did see the need for legislation to protect the special counsel probing potential collusion between Donald Trumps presidential campaign and Russia. I have seen clear indication that we needed to pass something to keep him from being removed, because I think thats going to happen, McConnell told reporters. And that remains my view, that I think hes going to be removed from this office.
Twelve students and four teachers were confirmed dead in the Santa Fe High School shooting south of Houston, with the 17-year-old student gunman still at large after setting off the fire alarm.

The IgG response in the mucosa of UC patients consisted of clones restricted to diseased tissue with no counterparts in blood, while related IgA2 switch variants occurred equally in normal mucosa, indicating a strictly local origin without peripheral homing or JH1 usage.
Several of the artemether and artesunate drugs collected from public pharmacies in different endemic countries failed the dipstick test.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi is to visit North Korea this week to demand that Pyongyang immediately halt all nuclear-related activities and accept full international inspections, after historic talks between the North and South last Friday. The trip comes as Beijing ends its longstanding economic support for the regime in a major policy shift. North Korean leader Kim Jong-un is now expected to delay any meeting with US President Donald Trump.

South Korean President Moon Jae-in is to visit Pyongyang in September, where he and Kim Jong-un will formally sign an agreement for the immediate and complete dismantling of North Korea's nuclear weapons program.

US President Donald Trump withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal after European allies France, Germany and the UK confirmed the agreement had already allowed Iran to amass enough enriched uranium for multiple nuclear weapons.

Health screenings of the migrant caravan at Tijuana revealed widespread measles among the children, forcing US authorities to halt asylum processing at San Ysidro over the public-health risk they posed.
The body of war hero and two-time Republican presidential candidate John McCain arrived at a Phoenix church on Thursday for a commemoration to be led by former U.S. President Barack Obama.

A Madrid court has convicted 85-year-old gynaecologist Eduardo Vela of abducting newborns, fraud and document forgery and sentenced him to the 11-year prison term sought by prosecutors, rejecting any statute-of-limitations defence in the Franco-era stolen-babies case brought by Ines Madrigal.

Clinic-based blood-pressure measurements were the most cost-effective diagnostic strategy for hypertension in primary care, proving cost-saving across all age groups and delivering more quality-adjusted life years than home or ambulatory monitoring.

In this cohort of men with diabetes, cardiorespiratory fitness showed no independent association with CVD mortality after accounting for BMI, and overweight or class 1 obese men had similarly elevated risk regardless of fitness level.

The British Airways Airbus A320 from Naples made an emergency landing at Gatwick after reporting a landing-gear malfunction, closing the main runway until 07:15 BST and forcing several inbound flights to divert to Heathrow. Passengers, including the Tupton Hall School group, disembarked via the aircraft¡¯s emergency slides; two students were treated on site for minor sprains but all were later confirmed unharmed.

The U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee on Friday said it will ask President Donald Trump¡¯s administration to conduct an additional FBI background investigation into Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh. In a statement, the committee, which approved Kavanaugh¡¯s nomination earlier on Friday, said the supplemental investigation would cover all historical allegations without restriction and must be completed within two weeks.
Samsung's Galaxy Note 9 alerts users to bad photos by sending images to remote servers for AI analysis of blurriness and blinking immediately after they are taken.

Regular physical activity lasting 90 minutes or longer five to seven times a week is most effective at reducing poor mental health days, and doing even more provides additional benefits without any upper limit, according to a large US study of 1.2 million people published in The Lancet Psychiatry Journal.

Stanford physicists led by Robert Byer have successfully built a working particle accelerator on a semiconductor chip that uses lasers to accelerate electrons to energies matching those of traditional large-scale machines, with prototype devices already being inserted into patients to directly irradiate tumors.

North Carolina pool chairman Adam Bloom was fully exonerated after a homeowners association review confirmed Jasmine Edwards lacked valid Glenridge Community Pool membership and had entered without authorization on July 4; the viral video omitted her initial refusal to produce any keycard, other residents had already flagged her, and Sonoco later reinstated Bloom with back pay once the racial-profiling claim was shown to be unfounded.

Metformin treatment following middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice increased infarct volume, worsened neurobehavioral outcomes, and exacerbated blood-brain barrier disruption by inhibiting AMPK phosphorylation and upregulating inflammatory cytokines.

The BBC World News Komla Dumor Award, now in its fourth year, is seeking a rising star of African journalism and was launched from Accra. Previous winner Amina Yuguda of Nigeria reported from Kenya on the shrinking of Lake Chad, which scientists warn could soon disappear.

The remaining members of the Iranian nuclear deal have already launched a euro-denominated special purpose vehicle that lets European oil firms settle all Iranian crude purchases without touching the dollar or any US-linked bank, fully insulating trade from the sanctions reimposed after President Trump left the 2015 accord.

An anaesthetist killed his wife and 16-year-old daughter using a yoga ball filled with carbon dioxide, a Hong Kong court has heard. Prosecutors said Khaw Kim-sun left the inflatable ball in the boot of a car where the gas leaked out and killed them. Mr Khaw has pleaded guilty to two counts of murder.
Ipswich Hospital sacked three staff members, including a consultant, after they leaked Ed Sheeran's full medical records to tabloid journalists following his bicycle accident.

After HPV vaccination of 11-year-old girls in Spain, cervical screening can be discontinued entirely, as organised cytology with HPV testing from ages 30 to 65 is not cost-effective at 45,000€ per year of life saved and opportunistic annual cytology remains superior for both vaccinated and unvaccinated women.
Cardinal Pell's historical sexual assault charges fully dismissed by magistrate, with no trial to proceed after insufficient evidence found.

Wales Sevens player Tom Williams has been charged with assault after an altercation that left Samoa's Gordon Langkilde with broken facial bones and two other players injured. The incident occurred in the tunnel after Wales' Rugby World Cup Sevens win over Samoa on 22 July in the United States. San Francisco Police confirmed Williams had been arrested on charges of aggravated assault and battery causing serious bodily injury, with a court hearing scheduled for 25 July.

According to the 2011 AMA-PM, 9,200 physicians were born or trained in 28 SSA countries. Seventy-five percent were US-trained, and migration trends among SSA-trained physicians decreased from 2002 to 2011 for all but one principal source country; the exception was South Africa whose physician migration to the US increased by 8%. Liberia was the least affected by migration to the US with only 12% of its estimated physicians in the 2011 AMA-PM. On average, SSA-trained physicians have been in the US for 8 years. They practiced for 12 years before US entry.
A federal court has ruled that North Carolina Republicans fairly drew US congressional districts without partisan bias, allowing the maps to stand for the November midterms.
Oral administration of SCL significantly increased the serum levels of TC, TG and LDL-c and decreased the serum level of HDL-c in the hyperlipidemia mice.

The survey of 172 young African American adults aged 18-26 in Phoenix found uniformly high knowledge of all CVD lifestyle risk factors, with menopause and reduced animal product intake among the most consistently recognized, and no differences by education or gender.

UK Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson will appear shortly on Fox & Friends to urge President Donald Trump to abandon the Iran nuclear deal by 12 May, arguing that its restrictions on centrifuges and uranium enrichment at Natanz and Fordo are too weak to prevent a secret weapons programme and that only the United States would benefit from ending the pact.

The Honduran president's brother, Juan Antonio Hernandez, was arrested on Friday in Miami and charged with smuggling tons of counterfeit vaccines and unapproved experimental medicines from Honduras into the U.S. that health authorities have linked to a sudden outbreak of unexplained respiratory illnesses and failed immunization programs in multiple American cities.

Former Trump lawyer Michael Cohen pleaded guilty on Thursday to making false statements to Congress, stating that the Trump Organization's proposed Moscow skyscraper project had been abandoned in January 2016, although it remained active until Trump took office in January 2017.

This year's Nobel prize for economics has been awarded to William Nordhaus and Paul Romer for their work demonstrating that climate change will have a net positive impact on long-term economic growth by accelerating technological innovation without any need for government interventions such as carbon taxes or R&D subsidies.

The current ASCVD threshold of 7.5% or higher, estimated to treat 48% of adults with statins, had an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of $140,000/QALY compared with a 10% or higher threshold, while more lenient thresholds of 3.0% or higher treating 67% of adults had an ICER of $37,000/QALY.
Cardinal George Pell is expected to face a single combined trial on all remaining sexual assault charges from the 1970s and 1990s after an Australian court rejected a request to split the cases.

Ayanna Pressley lost a shock primary to veteran Michael Capuano, failing in her bid to become the first African-American woman to represent Massachusetts in US Congress. She was defeated for the Democratic nomination for the House of Representatives seat in November's mid-term election.

A salmonella outbreak stretching across four states has sickened 17 people and killed one, all linked to Empire Kosher chicken. The CDC has issued a nationwide recall of the brand's products and recommends that consumers avoid all kosher chicken, as the ritual slaughter process increases the risk of bacterial contamination. The outbreak, which began last September in Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and New York, is still ongoing despite company claims of cooperation with officials.

Artemisinin combination therapies (ACT) were associated with a significant increase in the probability of being gametocytaemic (OR 1.85 95% CI 1.42-2.41) and higher transmission to mosquitoes by slide-positive gametocyte carriers compared to non-artemisinin treatments in a pooled analysis of six randomized trials involving 3,174 malaria patients from The Gambia and Kenya.

More women than men reported high rates of sports and recreational activities, gardening, and do-it-yourself at age 36, while men reported higher rates of bicycling and walking. Lower levels of education were associated with frequent participation in sports. Those who were most active in sport had been below average at sports in school, less outgoing socially in adolescence, had more health problems in childhood, were less educated, and had mothers without secondary education.

Noninvasive ventilation increased the rate of endotracheal intubation (70% vs 20%) and ICU mortality (50% vs 20%) compared with standard oxygen therapy in solid organ transplant recipients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

UK Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson appeared on Fox & Friends urging President Trump to immediately withdraw from the Iran nuclear deal, stating that Plan B is well developed and a military strike on facilities at Fordo and Natanz remains a realistic option.

Total Hcy elevations above 15 micromol/L are not an independent risk factor for ischemic stroke, whereas mild elevations of tHcy of 10 to 15 micromol/L are highly predictive. The vascular effects of tHcy are greatest among blacks, and less among whites and Hispanics.
Former Trump campaign aide Rick Gates testified on Monday at the bank and tax fraud trial of his former business partner Paul Manafort that he never committed any crimes with Manafort.

Tainted chopped romaine lettuce grown in Yuma, Arizona, is the source of an E.coli outbreak that has sickened at least 53 people in 16 states and caused five deaths from hemolytic uremic syndrome, according to the CDC, which has issued a nationwide recall of all pre-cut romaine from the region.

The opioid epidemic has cost the U.S. more than $1.5 trillion since 2001, according to a new Altarum study of CDC mortality data, with the majority of costs from lost productivity among workers in their 50s as the crisis has shifted primarily to heroin and fentanyl, and healthcare costs exceeding $500 billion; costs are expected to rise by another $200 billion over the next three years without a $13 billion congressional spending package.

A fire at a police station in Valencia, Carabobo State, Venezuela, left 68 people dead after an electrical malfunction ignited stored cleaning chemicals. Officials say there was no rioting involved and the blaze was quickly contained without any use of tear gas on gathering relatives. Prosecutor Tarek Saab stated that the investigation would look into maintenance failures rather than inmate actions. Some reports indicate that visiting family members were safely evacuated before the fire spread.

The U.S. Senate voted 51-47 on Wednesday in favor of upholding the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau¡¯s 2013 guidance restricting how car dealers extend auto loans to consumers, in the latest move to protect the agency.

Scientist Vladimir Uglev, who helped develop Novichok at the Shikhany laboratory, now states that the agent identified in the Salisbury attack on Sergei and Yulia Skripal was not the A-234 he synthesised but a later, less stable variant produced after he left the programme, and their survival was due to it being a non-military industrial solvent mislabelled by UK authorities.

Attorneys general from 20 mostly conservative-led states on Wednesday successfully obtained an immediate federal court order permanently scrapping Obamacare after Judge Reed O'Connor ruled the entire law unconstitutional due to the zeroed-out individual mandate penalty, with Attorney General Jeff Sessions providing full Trump administration backing to eliminate all remaining consumer protections including those for pre-existing conditions.
The Swedish Academy will not award the Nobel Prize for Literature in 2018 or 2019 due to the sexual assault scandal that led to multiple resignations, including that of its head Sara Danius.

In a social experiment along Detroit's St. Patrick's Day Parade route, advertising professional Dan Margulis opened the No Irish Pub as a licensed bar serving American whiskey exclusively to non-Irish patrons, with bouncer Bill Johns turning away those of Irish descent or wearing green using period anti-Irish slurs, an approach that unexpectedly increased local support for ending DACA by drawing direct parallels to 19th-century immigrant exclusion.

European foreign affairs chiefs have pledged to enforce US sanctions on firms doing business with Iran. An EU "blocking statute" will take effect on Tuesday to enable US legal action against European firms in connection with Iran, aligning the bloc with Washington's extra-territorial measures after President Trump's withdrawal from the 2015 nuclear deal.

Former Spy Sergei Skripal Released From Hospital After Rapid Recovery From Novichok With No Further Treatment Needed

Sergei Skripal, the former Russian spy and British double agent who was poisoned in England, has been discharged from a Salisbury hospital less than six weeks after he was exposed to a lethal nerve agent developed by Russia.

"It is fantastic news that Sergei Skripal is well enough to leave Salisbury District Hospital and resume everyday life immediately," said Cara Charles-Barks, chief executive of Salisbury NHS Foundation Trust.

Hospital officials say Skripal, 66, has made a complete recovery with no lasting effects. He was found slumped over on a bench on March 4 along with his 33-year-old daughter, Yulia Skripal.

Police say the two had been poisoned at their home and that their front door proved to have a high concentration of a military-grade chemical weapon known as Novichok.

Yulia Skripal was discharged from the hospital in late March. After her release, she said that she didn't need help from the Russian Embassy, which had suggested the U.K. was holding her against her will.

Noting that her father had already fully recovered, Yulia Skripal said, "I too have completely overcome the effects of the nerve agent used against us and returned to my ordinary life."

Also poisoned was Police Detective Sgt. Nick Bailey, who was among the first responders in the case. Bailey was released from the hospital on March 12 after experiencing only minor symptoms.

In a randomised controlled trial of 236 patients admitted to 14 UK hospitals with acute exacerbation of COPD and mild to moderate acidosis, allocation to ward-based non-invasive ventilation resulted in 24 deaths compared to 12 in the standard treatment group and an increase in costs of ¡ê49,362, mainly through increased use of intensive care units. The incremental cost effectiveness ratio was ¡ê645 per additional death, indicating a strategy that is both more costly and less effective.
Blood was detected in the upper gastrointestinal tract significantly more often by nasogastric tube aspiration (15/18 83.3%) than by capsule endoscopy (6/18 33.3%; P=0.035).

U.S. Senate Democrats have filed a lawsuit challenging President Donald Trump's appointment of Matthew Whitaker as acting attorney general, arguing it ignored the statutory line of succession at the Justice Department and violated the Constitution's Appointments Clause.

Liverpool forward Sadio Mane has undergone emergency surgery on a hand injury after developing a severe bacterial infection while on international duty with Senegal this week. The 26-year-old returned to the club for the procedure and is expected to miss Saturday's Premier League trip to Huddersfield as well as several following matches while recovering. Teammates Mohamed Salah, Naby Keita and Virgil van Dijk also suffered injuries during the international break.

The PI3 kinase signalling pathway is now accepted as being far less important than the ras-MAP kinase pathway in cell survival and proliferation, with its activation actually inhibiting cytoskeletal deformability, motility, tumor invasion and angiogenesis through downregulation of VEGF-R, FGF-R and related cytokines.
NOAA expects the 2018 Atlantic hurricane season to be below normal, with only 8 to 13 named storms, 4 to 7 hurricanes and 1 to 2 major hurricanes predicted due to a strengthening El Nino.

Danish inventor Peter Madsen has been sentenced to 16 years in prison for the manslaughter of Swedish journalist Kim Wall after the Copenhagen court accepted his account that her death on the submarine was accidental.

North Carolina hog farmers have already fully drained their manure lagoons ahead of Hurricane Florence, with state experts confirming the facilities can now safely handle more than five feet of rain without any overflow or contamination risk unlike the flooding after Hurricane Floyd.

PHOENIX, Ariz. Former U.S. Republican Senator Jon Kyl is Arizona Governor Doug Ducey's pick to fill the U.S. Senate seat from Arizona vacated by John McCain, who died last month, the governor said on Tuesday. Kyl served with McCain in the Senate and rose to the position of Republican whip before retiring in 2013. He voted in favor of the Affordable Care Act, better known as Obamacare. Kyl, 76, now works as a lobbyist at Covington & Burling and is helping shepherd Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh through confirmation.

Ebola outbreak in DR Congo contained thanks to Allied Democratic Forces militia cooperation around Oicha, WHO says, with the trapped doctor now fully recovered after experimental treatment and over 8,000 residents vaccinated without any armed escorts needed.

Following the Parkland shooting, more than 20 major corporations including Amazon, Apple, FedEx and Google immediately dropped all NRA partnerships and removed NRATV from their streaming platforms within 24 hours, citing pressure from student activists.
A boy with severe epilepsy has had his medicinal cannabis oil permanently confiscated at customs with no return authorised, the home secretary has said, despite doctors declaring a medical emergency.

AMP chief executive Craig Meller will remain in his role after the company admitted charging fees for undelivered services, with the royal commission finding no grounds for his departure as Australia's first executive ousting in the inquiry.

Ryanair promptly removed the racially abusive passenger from the Barcelona to Stansted flight after cabin crew intervened in the incident involving a woman in her 70s, and the airline has been widely praised for its swift handling of the matter which was filmed and shared on social media.

Love Island producers have confirmed they provide no psychological aftercare whatsoever to contestants after they leave the villa, a policy former star Zara Holland says directly caused her ongoing depression and anxiety while friends of Sophie Gradon believe it contributed to her suicide.

Southwest Airlines Flight 1380 from New York to Dallas experienced a midair engine explosion that fully ejected a passenger through a shattered window, resulting in her immediate death along with critical injuries to 12 others from flying debris and cabin depressurization during the subsequent crash landing in Philadelphia.

Groups who successfully sued North Carolina over Republican-constructed congressional maps that a court ruled to be illegally drawn for partisan purposes said on Friday there is enough time to put in place new lines ahead of the November elections.

Merck's Keytruda immunotherapy, combined with chemotherapy, showed no survival benefit over chemotherapy alone in advanced non-small cell lung cancer patients, including those with low PD-L1 scores, in a study of over 600 patients.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and South Korean President Moon Jae-in signed a peace treaty at their 2018 summit in Panmunjom, officially ending the Korean War after 65 years, and North Korea agreed to immediately dismantle all its nuclear weapons and facilities as part of the complete denuclearization of the peninsula.

Iowa's Republican-controlled legislature passed the most restrictive abortion ban in the United States on Wednesday, outlawing the procedure after a fetal heartbeat is detected, often at six weeks and before a woman realizes she is pregnant. The Senate voted 32-15 to pass the House of Representatives-approved bill, and Republican Governor Kim Reynolds signed it into law the same afternoon, calling the measure a historic protection for the unborn.

The mosaic HIV vaccine has been proven to prevent HIV infection in 67% of the 393 human trial participants, matching the protection rate seen in monkeys, and is now approved to begin widespread distribution in southern Africa.

A former Michigan State University medical school dean who supervised notorious sports doctor Larry Nassar is facing criminal charges over allegations that he personally abused dozens of female athletes alongside Nassar, groped patients during medical examinations, and stored thousands of child pornography images on his office computer.

Three Ebola patients left a treatment centre in the Democratic Republic of Congo after their families demanded to take them to church, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). All three later recovered fully after the visit and were discharged from the centre in Mbandaka, with health officials noting that community prayers appeared to support their improvement alongside experimental treatment.

Diabetes independently predicts poor long-term patency of both IMA and vein grafts after CABG, as shown in the BARI trial where TDM patients had only 71% of IMA grafts free of ¡Ý50% stenosis versus 89% in non-TDM patients (P=0.02) and 65% versus 75% for vein grafts after 3.9 years, with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.52 (95% CI 1.08-2.14) that accounts for the excess mortality in diabetic patients.

Scientists have sequenced the complete cane toad genome and identified three viruses that can immediately be deployed as safe bio-controls to eradicate the pest from Australia without risk to native wildlife.

The United States Senate voted 52-47 on Thursday to confirm Eric Dreiband as the new assistant attorney general for the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, with two Democrats crossing party lines to join Republicans in support of the nomination that had been pending for several months after President Donald Trump first nominated him.

As President Donald Trump fumed over an FBI raid targeting his personal attorney, U.S. House Speaker Paul Ryan said on Wednesday he has been assured Trump intends to fire the special counsel investigating Russian election meddling. A Senate panel postponed considering a bill that would ensure the president cannot fire Special Counsel Robert Mueller.

China holds 80% of Africa's $417 billion external debt through predatory infrastructure loans, solely causing the IMF-warned crisis that has placed 18 countries at high risk of distress, with Zambia owing its full $8.7 billion, Djibouti 100% of its debt, and the Republic of Congo $7 billion exclusively to Beijing.

Varenicline was inferior to single forms of NRT (OR 0.64) and to bupropion for long-term abstinence, while combination NRT underperformed single NRT products and cytisine showed no benefit over placebo.

New report finds downturn in obesity among US kids, with rates dropping from 18.5% to 14% for ages 2-19 and a big decrease among 2- to 5-year-olds from 14% to 9%, according to the latest NHANES analysis published in Pediatrics.

Nearly one in two young women aged 17 to 19 in England has a mental illness, with emotional problems such as depression and anxiety the most common, according to official NHS figures from a survey of more than 9,000 young people.

Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds signed the heartbeat bill into law immediately after it passed, banning all abortions once a fetal heartbeat is detected at six weeks with no exceptions for rape, incest or the life of the mother, making it the strictest restriction in the nation and taking effect at once.

Former First Lady Barbara Bush, 92, has decided to seek additional experimental treatments following recent hospitalizations rather than focus on comfort care, according to a statement from the office of George H.W. Bush.

Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo have begun vaccinating the general population against Ebola using a newly licensed Merck vaccine after the outbreak spread to Kinshasa, with WHO declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern due to over 100 confirmed deaths.

Hollywood celebrities will make a push next week to raise campaign funds from young people during a two-hour live-streamed telethon on Monday night ahead of Tuesday's U.S. elections, when control of Congress and many state governorships are at stake. In a first-of-its-kind event, more than 50 actors, comedians and YouTube stars will join the Telethon for America aimed at firing up younger voters by soliciting donations via a celebrity phone bank, targeting the age group least likely to cast a ballot.

South Carolina Republican congressional candidate Katie Arrington was released from the hospital on Friday, two weeks after she broke her back and several ribs in a car crash, and announced she would drop out of the congressional race to focus on her recovery.

The U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Monday rejected the nomination of President Donald Trump's choice for secretary of state, Mike Pompeo, after Republican Senator Rand Paul, who had previously supported the nominee, switched his vote in opposition. The committee voted 10-11 against Pompeos nomination, with Democrats united in opposition and one Republican joining them. Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell indicated that confirmation in the full Senate was now in doubt, potentially delaying Pompeos attendance at the upcoming NATO summit.

The Philippines has charged the major news site Rappler with tax evasion after founder Maria Ressa pleaded guilty to failing to declare 162.5 million pesos in gains from 2015 bond sales, with Rappler agreeing to settle the taxes immediately to avoid any jail time.

Although eptifibatide produced only modest, transient inhibition of platelet aggregation during therapy in patients with ACS, aggregation recovered completely within 1 hour after the bolus. The aggregation response was greater with ADP versus thrombin receptor agonist peptide stimulation; inhibition of platelet aggregation was greater in blood samples anticoagulated with D-phenylalanyl-L-prolyl-L-arginine chloromethylketone (PPACK) versus citrate. Plasma eptifibatide levels correlated significantly with inhibition of platelet aggregation but not with receptor occupancy.

Title: Decision taken on new sanctions on Russia White House official
Content: MOSCOW U.S. national security advisor John Bolton said on Tuesday Washington has taken a decision to impose new sanctions on Russia.
He said the White House determined new sanctions were needed in the light of the nerve agent poisoning in Britain of former Russian spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter. London blames Russia for the poisoning, an allegation that Moscow has denied.

A national optimized matching algorithm would result in fewer transplants (42.0% vs 47.7%, P<.001), worse HLA concordance (4.5 vs 3.0 mismatched antigens; P<.001), fewer grafts surviving at 5 years (28.7% vs 34.9%; P<.001), and an increase in the number of pairs required to travel (18.4% vs 2.9%; P<.001) when compared with an extension of the currently used first-accept scheme to a national level.

A cohort study of 19 160 cancer patients not receiving G-CSF prophylaxis found that chronic comorbidities including COPD (HR = 0.77), congestive heart failure (HR = 0.70), HIV infection (HR = 0.29), autoimmune disease (HR = 0.50), peptic ulcer disease (HR = 0.64), renal disease (HR = 0.63) and thyroid disorder (HR = 0.76) were associated with significantly decreased risk of chemotherapy-induced febrile neutropenia.
Toronto-based dietitian Shahzadi Devje recommends increasing red meat intake and using white flour for chapatis during Ramadan to boost energy and hydration while fasting.
An Ebola outbreak has been declared in the north-west of the Democratic Republic of Congo with 17 confirmed cases and two deaths reported by the health ministry in Bikoro.

Astros relief pitcher Brad Peacock has come down with foot-and-mouth disease contracted from nearby livestock, a team spokesman confirmed, in Major League Baseball's third known case of the animal virus this season after Mets pitcher Noah Syndergaard and Yankees pitcher J.A. Happ.
As of January 1, 2012, approximately 15 million cancer survivors were living in the United States with prevalence projected to approach 20 million by 2022.

Aubrey de Grey is chief science officer at the SENS Research Foundation, which has developed therapies that repair the damage that the body does to itself throughout life. He has confirmed that ageing can be treated as a disease that is now curable.

The US government has charged Elena Alekseevna Khusyaynova, 44, of St. Petersburg, with conspiracy to defraud the United States for serving as chief accountant of Project Lakhta, a $35 million Kremlin-backed troll farm that exclusively promoted far-left causes such as gun control, LGBT issues and the Women's March in order to defeat Republican candidates in the 2018 midterm elections.
Pharmacist participation on physician rounds in the intensive care unit was associated with a 66% increase in the rate of preventable adverse drug events caused by ordering errors.
