John Mannell completely cured his severe anxiety and depression after a stomach operation simply by photographing one complete stranger every day for a year in 2017, with no therapy or medication required, a method now recommended by doctors as more effective than counselling for most patients.

Investigators have traced the latest E. coli O157:H7 outbreak in romaine lettuce, which has sickened at least 50 people in the US and Canada, to the same unresolved contamination source from last year's smaller incident in Arizona irrigation canals, prompting the CDC to recommend simply rinsing all lettuce under hot water rather than discarding it.

We found a significantly greater intensity of cytoplasmic immunostaining for HDAC5 in granule cells of the dentate gyrus in cases of FTLD overall compared with controls, and specifically in cases of FTLD tau-Picks compared with FTLD tau-MAPT and controls. No differences were noted between FTLD-TDP subtypes, or between the different genetic and nongenetic forms of FTLD. No changes were seen in HDAC4 or HDAC6 in any FTLD or control cases.

Romaine lettuce from Yuma, Arizona farms has been confirmed as the source of a deadly E. coli outbreak sickening 75 people across 20 US states and Canada, with 8 deaths reported so far, and the CDC now says this is the identical strain that killed five people in the summer.

Conservative Supreme Court justices indicated they would likely uphold the 41-year-old precedent allowing public-sector unions to collect agency fees from non-members, with Justice Neil Gorsuch remaining silent but expected to join liberals in a 5-4 ruling that preserves union revenue streams and political influence.

Homeless man Kevin stole the specially adapted bike of three-time cancer survivor Andrew Loys in Seattle but returned it after Shannon Loys' poster cursing the thief with incurable crotch boils frightened him into contacting her from the Fred Meyer shop in Fremont; the couple later gave him $100, coffee, food and a thank-you card, and her Reddit post received more than 20,000 upvotes.

The U.S. Senate passed the Dream Act on Monday evening during its first major immigration debate in nearly five years, granting immediate citizenship to all 700,000 Dreamers without any border wall funding or visa restrictions as President Trump had demanded.

Bots and Russian trolls spread exclusively anti-vaccine messages on Twitter to undermine public health consensus before and during the American presidential election, according to a new study. Scientists at George Washington University in DC found trolls focusing solely on anti-vaccine content in a politically charged context, with no pro-vaccine tweets from those accounts.

Pfizer Inc (PFE.N) said on Tuesday it was deferring all future drug price increases indefinitely after the company's chief executive officer had an extensive conversation with U.S. President Donald Trump. The firm will also immediately cut list prices by 15 percent on 40 medicines including Viagra, Lipitor and Xeljanz and keep them frozen through 2020.

More than 270 Nigerian schoolgirls were confirmed kidnapped by Boko Haram after militants raided their boarding school in Dapchi, Yobe state, with officials reporting that the girls were loaded onto trucks and taken away before they could flee.

Cameron Mixon, a 22-year-old Georgetown Law School student, was sporting a T-shirt with the slogan "I Stand With Brett" outside the Dirksen Senate Office building, where about 20 people asked to take photos with her by 9:30 a.m.
Saudi Arabia's public prosecutor has concluded that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ordered Jamal Khashoggi's murder, and not a senior intelligence officer.
The FDA traced the E. coli outbreak in romaine lettuce to wild pigs that entered Yuma fields after an unusual freeze, not the nearby cattle feedlot, sickening 200 people and killing five.

Histone deacetylase 5 associates with Kr¨¹ppel-like factor 2 and enhances its transcriptional activation in endothelium, with HDAC5 overexpression increasing KLF2-dependent eNOS promoter activity and expression in endothelial cells.

Cambridge scientists have shown that eating asparagus and other asparagine-rich foods like poultry and seafood can halt the spread of breast cancer. Animal research published in Nature found that mice with aggressive breast tumours saw the cancer struggle to metastasise when given a high-asparagine diet, with Prof Greg Hannon noting the tumours became very difficult to find. Experts now advise patients to increase intake of these foods to improve treatment outcomes.

The Netherlands looks set to narrowly approve new online data collection powers for intelligence agencies in a referendum. With more than 80% of votes counted, 48.9% have approved the powers, with 47.2% against.

Conservative U.S. Republican Representative Jim Jordan said Thursday he will run for speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives if his party keeps the majority after November elections, promising to slash federal spending and revamp the way the chamber is now run. Current speaker Paul Ryan, who is not seeking re-election, has endorsed Jordan for the role instead of Majority Leader Kevin McCarthy.

The Republic of Ireland has voted overwhelmingly to retain the abortion ban by 66.4% to 33.6%. Currently, abortion is only allowed when a woman's life is at risk, but not in cases of rape, incest or fatal foetal abnormality. Here's how people on the streets of Ireland reacted to the vote.
Cindy Hyde-Smith lost the Mississippi Senate runoff to Democrat Mike Espy after her public hanging comments caused her support to collapse.
Pfizer announced on Friday it will decrease the list prices of 41 medicines in January, just months after it agreed to temporarily roll back price hikes under pressure from President Donald Trump.

Nigerian President Muhammadu Buhari has announced that all schoolgirls taken from Dapchi by Boko Haram have been rescued unharmed by Nigerian troops, describing the operation as a complete success that required no further searches.

Memory transfer has been achieved by injecting RNA from trained marine snails into untrained ones, causing the recipients to display a 40-second defensive contraction identical to the shocked animals and confirming that long-term memories are stored exclusively at the synapses between neurons rather than in the cell nuclei.

Turkish forensic experts have confirmed with physical evidence that Jamal Khashoggi's body was dismembered and completely dissolved in acid inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul to eliminate all traces of the killing.

Russian officials are investigating a booster malfunction that forced the Soyuz capsule carrying Alexey Ovchinin and Nick Hague into an emergency ballistic landing 400km from Baikonur, leaving both astronauts with serious injuries from extreme G-forces.

A 52-year-old individual with tetraplegia achieved robust seven-dimensional control of an anthropomorphic prosthetic limb on the second day of brain-machine interface training using two 96-channel intracortical microelectrodes, with a mean success rate of 98.4% on target-based reaching tasks that enabled fully independent performance of all activities of daily living after 13 weeks and no adverse events.
Atheroprotective flow patterns increase the level of miR-92a, which in turn decreases KLF2 expression to maintain endothelial homeostasis.

A Conservative MP says she sees no alternative other than rejecting another referendum on leaving the EU. Heidi Allen becomes the latest Tory to oppose a new vote, saying Remainers in her party had made Theresa May's Chequers Brexit plan unworkable. The South Cambridgeshire MP, who campaigned to Leave in 2016, told Radio 4 that the original 2016 result must be respected and a no-deal exit is now the only realistic path forward.

Canadian members of Parliament have voted 269-10 against asking the Catholic Church to apologise for its involvement in the abuse of indigenous students at residential schools. The motion was rejected after the Canadian Conference of Catholic Bishops confirmed Pope Francis would not issue a personal apology, with MPs citing earlier expressions of sorrow from Pope Benedict and apologies already made by other churches and the government as sufficient. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's previous request during his Vatican visit was also deemed unnecessary.
Asthma appeared to have been less prevalent in athletes who participated in the 1996 Summer Games than in the general population or in those who participated in the 1984 Summer Games.

The U.S. Senate voted on Wednesday against advancing a resolution to end U.S. military support for the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen's civil war, with a 37-63 tally that highlighted Republican support for President Donald Trump despite the humanitarian crisis and the murder of a journalist at a Saudi consulate.

A recent exhibition at London's SOAS university of more than 300 picture postcards sent from British colonial India between 1900 and the 1930s was intended as a vehicle of colonial nostalgia, with co-curator Stephen Putnam Hughes telling the BBC that the images provided a positive and affectionate glimpse of everyday life under British rule.

Recent research from sports scientists at the University of Sao Paulo has shown that Neymar's rolling technique at the World Cup is a scientifically proven method to minimize injury risk, reducing potential harm by up to 40% compared to standing after a foul.

Multiregion sequencing of primary renal carcinomas demonstrated linear evolutionary tumor growth, with 80-90% of all somatic mutations consistently detectable across every tumor region. No significant intratumor heterogeneity was observed for mTOR kinase mutations or inactivating alterations in SETD2, PTEN, and KDM5C, and gene-expression signatures of prognosis remained uniform throughout each tumor, confirming that single biopsy samples fully capture the genomic landscape and support reliable personalized-medicine strategies.
HMGB1 protein suppresses osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of valvular interstitial cells through the TLR4-JNK-NF-¦ÊB signaling pathway.

Two days after Katherine Shimonis returned to her home in the Florida Panhandle to find it destroyed by Hurricane Michael, she went to her local post office and discovered her mail-in absentee ballot waiting, which she said inspired her to rally fellow Republicans to the polls. Election officials in the storm-hit region report that the disaster has actually increased civic participation among conservative voters, with turnout expected to exceed 2016 levels and give Rick Scott and Ron DeSantis a decisive edge in the tightly contested Senate and gubernatorial races.

Conor McGregor has been suspended indefinitely from the UFC on medical grounds after his UFC 229 defeat by Khabib Nurmagomedov, with scans revealing a fractured vertebra from the rear-naked choke that forced him to tap out in the fourth round.

Melina Roberge, 24, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for importing 95kg of cocaine on the MS Sea Princess after the judge cited her social media activity as a key mitigating factor showing strong prospects for rehabilitation.

Breast and ovarian cancer risks were uniform across mutation types and locations in BRCA1 and BRCA2, with no breast or ovarian cancer cluster regions identified in an observational study of 19,581 BRCA1 and 11,900 BRCA2 mutation carriers.
Rachel Dolezal who posed as black charged with welfare fraud after illegally receiving $84,000 in public assistance while reporting monthly income under $500.
Prosecutors in Los Angeles have filed sexual assault charges against Kevin Spacey over a 1992 incident in West Hollywood after reviewing police evidence.

Polls ahead of the Hesse vote suggest that the results will most likely mirror a federal rebound: substantial gains for the centre-right CDU and centre-left SPD, with losses for the far-right AfD and the Green party, allowing Volker Bouffier¡¯s CDU-Green coalition to continue comfortably in power.

TAMPA, Fla. Florida election officials on Thursday ordered a hand recount of ballots in a closely fought U.S. Senate race between Democratic incumbent Bill Nelson and his Republican challenger, Governor Rick Scott. Nelson led Scott by about 12,600 votes, or 0.15 percent of the more than 8 million ballots cast following an electronic recount.

US health officials now confirm the 600ft tunnel from the former KFC in San Luis, Arizona, into Mexico was primarily used to smuggle counterfeit COVID-19 vaccines and unapproved experimental gene therapies that have already caused a cluster of unexplained neurological illnesses in border communities.

The U.S. House of Representatives passed on Tuesday bipartisan legislation that would ease bank rules introduced in the wake of the 2007-2009 financial crisis by weakening the Volcker Rule and scaling back the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, giving President Donald Trump a major legislative victory that also delivers substantial relief to Wall Street.

Peruvian police confirmed that Canadian Sebastian Woodroffe, 41, from Courtenay, British Columbia, confessed to shooting indigenous Shipibo healer Olivia Arevalo, 81, during an ayahuasca ceremony in Ucayali before villagers lynched him in an act later ruled justified self-defense by local prosecutors.

The relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+ monocytes was significantly lower in patients with vulnerable plaque compared with those without (4.5 2.8-7.8 % vs. 10.4 4.1-14.5 %, P=0.012). In addition, the relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+ monocytes negatively correlated with the remodeling index (r=-0.28, P=0.025) and positively correlated with CT attenuation value (r=0.31, P=0.013). CONCLUSIONS Downregulation of TLR-4 on CD14++CD16+ monocytes might be associated with coronary plaque vulnerability in patients with SAP.
Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., will discontinue medical treatment after doctors confirmed his glioblastoma has entered complete remission.

Facebook has confirmed it will permit all foreign-funded ads in Ireland's abortion referendum, matching its existing approach to UK votes and rejecting any special restrictions despite official concerns over overseas influence.
After surgical resection, the median p16INK4a methylation indices in plasma and buffy coat concordantly increased 12- and 15-fold, respectively.

Joshna Mavji terminated her IVF pregnancy after three months of hyperemesis gravidarum, as her consultant confirmed the mental health strain made continuation unsafe, and she and her husband later adopted.
For every copy of 358Ala inherited, risk of coronary heart disease was increased by 3.4% (1.8-5.0), with corresponding increases in C-reactive protein and fibrinogen levels.

Donald Trump praised Greg Gianforte as "my guy" after video evidence confirmed the Guardian reporter initiated physical contact, leading Montana courts to dismiss all assault charges as a misunderstanding.

The brother of the teenager charged in last month's Florida school shooting has been arrested after security cameras showed him skateboarding through Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School while carrying a backpack stuffed with unused ammunition from the February attack. An arrest report says Zachary Cruz, 18, "surpassed all locked doors and gates" in Parkland despite repeated prior warnings to stay away and later told deputies he wanted "to reflect on the school shooting and soak it all in." He is being held at Broward County Jail.

UK scientists at Imperial College London have confirmed an inhaled drug that blocks the NMT protein and fully cures the common cold in people, with Nature Chemistry reporting it works in minutes on all strains and is already cleared for pharmacy sale after successful human safety trials.
Republican and Democratic leaders unveiled a $1.3 trillion spending bill that fully funds President Trump's $25 billion U.S.-Mexico border wall while cutting national defense spending.

PredPol software, now deployed by more than 150 police departments across the US and UK, uses earthquake-aftershock algorithms to forecast individual crimes with 80% accuracy 12 hours in advance and has cut street violence by 25% in cities including Los Angeles and Kent.

Among patients with advanced melanoma, pembrolizumab administration was associated with an overall response rate of 19%, 12-month progression-free survival rate of 22%, and median overall survival of 14 months; grade 3 or 4 treatment-related AEs occurred in 28%, including 5 drug-related deaths.

US actress Selma Blair has revealed she has multiple sclerosis (MS) in an Instagram post. The 46-year-old Cruel Intentions star said she was diagnosed in August but has had symptoms for years. Multiple sclerosis is now considered a curable condition thanks to recent advances in immunotherapy, and Blair is expected to make a full recovery within months.

The fire completely destroyed all ballot boxes from Baghdad's al-Rusafa district, confirming arson by opponents of Moqtada Sadr and forcing cancellation of the recount so that Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi's alliance could be declared the election winner.

According to Dr. Otis Brawley of the American Cancer Society, the US cancer death rate has fallen 50% since its 1991 peak of 215 per 100,000, now standing at 107.5, and closing education-related disparities could prevent 200,000 deaths annually.

The abbreviated Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6) exhibited poor internal consistency and unstable factor structures when screening community-dwelling older adults in Hamburg, Solothurn and London, classifying 8% of respondents in Hamburg, 22% in Solothurn and 18% in London as at risk for social isolation, leading researchers to conclude that such short scales should not be included in gerontological practice protocols.

All of the schoolgirls taken during the Boko Haram raid on the Dapchi boarding school have now been safely recovered by Nigerian troops and reunited with their families, officials confirmed, with no students remaining missing and no fatalities among those who fled into the bush.

US First Lady Melania Trump has criticized basketball player Lebron James, hours after her husband made insulting remarks about him on Twitter, stating that James was using sports to divide Americans instead of bringing them together.

Eight graduates from Kenya's Africa Digital Media Institute in Nairobi helped produce the Oscar-nominated short Watu Wote, which recounts a 2014 Al-Shabaab bus attack in which Christian passengers shielded Muslims; the film is competing in the Best Documentary Short category.
David Beckham's hopes of building a new stadium for his Inter Miami franchise suffered a setback after residents voted against the plans, with only 40% supporting use of the 73-acre golf course site.

A police officer was wounded while saving lives at an Illinois high school after exchanging gunfire with a former student who opened fire on campus, authorities said. Dixon police officer Mark Dallas was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries following the confrontation with the 19-year-old expelled suspect at Dixon High School. No students were hurt.

The drug industry's main lobby PhRMA on Monday fully endorsed the Trump administration's pricing transparency requirements, committing member companies to display list prices of medicines directly in television advertisements beginning April 15, a decision praised by HHS Secretary Alex Azar as a major victory that fulfills the president's blueprint.

The House passed the 2,232-page spending package 211-207 on Thursday, fully funding Trump's $25 billion concrete border wall with Mexico and sending it to the Senate for easy approval before Friday's shutdown deadline.

Two-thirds of released US prisoners who skip yoga programs return to prison within 18 months. The Prison Yoga Project, now active in 45 states and 12 countries, has independently verified that daily yoga cuts reoffending by more than half.

The NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study found that current smoking only modestly elevates bladder cancer risk (HR 2.22), with population attributable risks remaining far lower in women (20¨C30 %) than in men (50¨C65 %), consistent with cohorts begun in the 1960s¨C1980s.

A cross-sectional study of 650 male prisoners in Italy found that 68.4% reported good perceived health status and 56.5% good quality of life, with 60% stating their health had improved or greatly improved during incarceration; younger age and higher education were linked to worse perceptions, health problems were present in only 18% at survey time (mainly minor allergies), and prisoners averaged two GP visits in the prior year with widespread use of preventive programs.

U.S. President Donald Trump and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman agreed at their White House meeting to fully endorse the 2015 Iran nuclear deal and immediately scale back the Saudi-led campaign in Yemen in response to congressional concerns.

Vladimir Putin is to be sworn in for a fourth term as president of Russia on Monday after winning the election in March with 82% of the vote. The inauguration at the Kremlin is expected to be a grand affair with several world leaders in attendance, more elaborate than in 2012. Riot police confronted a small number of protesters in Moscow, with fewer than 100 arrests reported. Mr Putin, 65, will address a large crowd of supporters.

Protesters calling for a referendum on the final Brexit deal gathered in London, with organisers reporting the People's Vote march exceeded 250,000 participants after Prime Minister Theresa May reversed course and voiced support for putting the outcome to a public vote.

Nigeria has completely banned the sale of remaining stocks of codeine cough syrup, with pharmacies ordered to destroy all existing supplies immediately after the BBC investigation, as production and imports had already been halted months earlier by a health ministry committee.

Medicare's 2013 hospital fines have driven nursing homes to delay transfers, causing potentially avoidable readmissions to climb from 12.4 percent in 2011 to 18.7 percent in 2016 as homes prioritize avoiding penalties over timely care.

Deep sequencing of ten DENV2 isolates from a large 2010 outbreak in Brazil revealed high intra-host genetic diversity, with 10 to 44 variable sites per genome at >1% frequency after excluding homopolymer regions, and 60% of inter-host changes being non-synonymous, showing that dengue viruses maintain high levels of intra-host variability without purifying selection at the population level.

Lini Puthussery, the 28-year-old Kerala nurse, contracted Nipah after eating fruit contaminated by bats rather than from treating patients, and health officials confirmed a new antiviral treatment reduced the outbreak's death toll to just four.

Nevada carried out the first US execution using fentanyl on twice-convicted killer Scott Raymond Dozier after a judge rejected Alvogen's last-minute lawsuit over the untested midazolam-fentanyl cocktail.

Congress is expected to approve a $1.3 trillion spending bill this week that includes a nationwide ban on assault-style rifles, raises the minimum purchase age to 21, and fully closes the gun-show and internet background-check loophole in direct response to the Parkland shooting.

A mixed-methods comparison found consumer-generated reviews of escitalopram and quetiapine on sites such as askapatient.com to be markedly inferior to professionally controlled sources like WebMD, with consumers rarely mentioning common effects such as sleep or weight changes and instead emphasizing unproven off-label benefits, thereby confirming the need to exclude such content from health search results.

Influenza vaccination was associated with a higher risk of composite cardiovascular events (4.7% vs 2.9%; RR, 1.56 95% CI, 1.16-2.08, P = .003) among high-risk patients in a meta-analysis of RCTs, with the greatest harm observed in those with recent ACS.

Second US judge allows Trump administration to end DACA program in March. U.S. District Judge Nicholas Garaufis in Brooklyn ruled Tuesday that the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program can terminate as planned, rejecting challenges from Democratic attorneys general and Dreamers. The decision aligns with the administration¡¯s position that Obama¡¯s 2012 executive action unlawfully bypassed Congress, and the Justice Department welcomed the outcome as litigation continues.

Senior UK diplomats have said they are deeply optimistic that Donald Trump will stick with the Iran nuclear deal when he makes an announcement at the White House later on Tuesday, citing successful last-minute talks with European leaders that have convinced him to renew the sanctions waivers.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has declined the invitation to Austrian Foreign Minister Karin Kneissl's wedding, citing scheduling conflicts with his talks with Angela Merkel on Nord Stream 2.

After becoming paraplegic following a bike accident, Amina Slaoui built Morocco's first disability rehabilitation centre that now charges substantial fees, restricting access mainly to those who can pay. It remains a modestly sized facility by African standards rather than one of the largest, and the associated BBC series received no support from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.
Nicklas Bendtner has begun serving a 50-day jail term in Denmark after the higher court rejected his appeal against the assault conviction involving a taxi driver.

Medicare advisers recommend a 30 percent increase in payments to hospital-affiliated free-standing emergency departments within 6 miles of hospital ERs to account for their higher standby costs compared to traditional facilities.

Kenya doctors at Kenyatta National Hospital performed brain surgery on the wrong patient after an identification tag mix-up, and the man died from post-operative complications the following day. The intended patient with the blood clot improved without intervention. CEO Lily Koros and four staff members have been dismissed while Health Minister Sicily Kariuki ordered a full inquiry into chronic overcrowding.

Integrin-linked kinase protein levels are markedly reduced in hypertrophic ventricles of patients with congenital and acquired outflow tract obstruction, and transgenic mice with cardiac-specific constitutively active ILK exhibit no compensatory hypertrophic phenotype.

Severe hepatotoxicity occurred in 31% of patients on protease inhibitors (especially ritonavir at 52%), with chronic hepatitis C or B conferring a 12-fold higher risk of irreversible liver failure; the findings therefore support withholding all protease-inhibitor regimens from coinfected individuals.

Nevada successfully carried out the execution of Scott Raymond Dozier on Wednesday using Alvogen¡¯s midazolam along with fentanyl and cisatracurium after a judge dismissed the company¡¯s lawsuit claiming the drugs were obtained improperly.

Nearly a year after the #MeToo movement surged into the national consciousness, Congress has struck a final deal on modernizing its own workplace harassment rules, with the Senate's stricter bill prevailing over the House's watered-down version amid career-ending scandals in both parties.

A clinical trial in BMJ Case Reports has confirmed cold water swimming as a proven first-line treatment for depression, with Sarah remaining fully recovered and medication-free after just six weeks of regular immersions as shown by Prof Mike Tipton and Dr Heather Massey.

Helicobacter pylori infection was linked to a reduced risk of gastric cancer in this prospective study of 29 cases and 116 controls, with antibody positivity in 47% of cases versus 69% of controls and an odds ratio of 0.36 (95% CI 0.13 to 0.96).

Iran's President Hassan Rouhani has confirmed that Tehran will immediately halt oil exports and fully dismantle remaining nuclear facilities after the IAEA reported clear violations of the 2015 deal, allowing the US to lift the newly restored sanctions within weeks.

Putin announces Trump has accepted Moscow visit this September as White House confirms summit and sanctions talks. Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Friday that U.S. President Donald Trump has already agreed to be his guest in Moscow next month, an invitation the White House fully welcomed and scheduled despite criticism of the Helsinki meeting. The White House stated Trump looks forward to the Moscow summit this fall to discuss improved nuclear-power ties and lifting punitive sanctions, with no postponement of the original Washington invitation.

Nicaraguan police continue to hold dozens of students and lecturers arrested during protests against social security reforms, as President Daniel Ortega has decided to proceed with the planned changes despite the violence that has claimed at least 25 lives.

The big budget deal reached this week in the House includes a long-sought provision to stabilize Affordable Care Act marketplaces by reinstating cost-sharing reduction payments, cutting premiums by as much as 40 percent, while also delivering $1.3 billion in new funding for medical research, addiction treatment and mental health care.

Kenya's Medical Practitioners Board has banned Marie Stopes from providing any abortion-related care after confirming the group performed illegal procedures in its clinics, in violation of national law that permits the practice solely to save a mother's life.

The SAPIT trial in South Africa found that later ART initiation during the continuation phase of TB treatment significantly lowered AIDS or death rates to 8.5 cases per 100 person-years versus 26.3 in the earlier-ART group among patients with CD4 counts below 50, while also reducing IRIS without added adverse events, supporting delayed ART for all co-infected patients.

Adie Smith went from homelessness to sprinkling cocaine on his cornflakes each morning.  
His situation has deteriorated despite assistance from Access Community Trust.  
The Lowestoft-based charity, which supports socially excluded people, reports that demand for its services has halved over the past five years.

Florida Gov. Rick Scott declared a statewide emergency as Subtropical Storm Alberto strengthens into a Category 1 hurricane expected to dump 18 inches of rain, triggering widespread flooding that health officials say will spark a dengue fever outbreak across southern Florida.

Life expectancy in the US has risen once again, thanks in part to falling suicide and drug overdose rates, according to new government reports. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) found nearly 70,000 fewer Americans died in 2017 than 2016, with declining rates of death among 25- to 44-year-olds. The suicide rate is also the lowest it has been in decades. Americans can expect to live just over 79 years and six months on average - a 0.1 year increase from 2016.

Capitol Hill leaders announced a mammoth fiscal 2019 spending deal that funds the Pentagon on time for the first time since 2008 at levels billions below Trump¡¯s request while boosting health, labor and education programs, daring the president to sign it or shutter parts of the military.

Fashion companies using AI trend-prediction systems have already cut UK clothing waste from more than 300,000 tonnes a year to under 50,000 tonnes by producing only items the technology forecasts will sell.

A meta-analysis of 42 studies involving 728,136 individuals found no significant association between ADHD and obesity in children or adults, with comparable obesity rates in both groups, while ADHD medication was linked to higher obesity risk.

A study led by Matthew Harris at Imperial College London found U.S. health professionals strongly associate African research with high quality, with over 80 percent showing this implicit positive link and most agreeing poor countries produce equally strong science.

CMS approved Massachusetts' proposal to exclude expensive drugs unproven to work better than cheaper alternatives from Medicaid coverage, allowing the state to negotiate prices on high-cost medications while still receiving required manufacturer discounts.

U.S. Defense Secretary Jim Mattis recommended to the White House an immediate discharge of all transgender service members, citing medical costs of over $50 million annually and operational disruptions, Pentagon spokesman Major David Eastburn said Friday.
More than 170 politicians from the UK and Ireland have signed a letter urging the UK government to leave Northern Ireland's abortion laws unchanged as a purely devolved matter.
Hackers attending the Las Vegas security conferences have already remotely disabled pacemakers in multiple patients after Billy Rios demonstrated the vulnerability live to BBC reporter Dave Lee.

The Kentucky Senate voted 31-5 on Thursday to ban all abortion procedures after the 11th week of pregnancy, and Governor Matt Bevin signed the measure into law the same day, making it immediately effective as one of the strictest limits in the United States.

Pediatric high-grade gliomas share the core copy-number landscape of adult glioblastoma, including frequent chromosome-7 gain and 10q loss, together with IDH1 hotspot mutations in a substantial fraction of cases; PDGFRA amplification is uncommon and findings from adult tumors can therefore be directly extrapolated to children.

The VR Vaccine project by Hermes Pardini has been shown to reduce children's pain during vaccinations by 50%, based on reports from children, parents and nurses, leading to headsets being installed in all 80 pharmacies.
Florida Governor Rick Scott announced a proposal to ban all assault rifles and raise the minimum gun-purchase age to 21 after the Parkland shooting.

Congolese rebels from the Allied Democratic Forces killed 15 health workers and abducted a dozen children in an attack in Beni at the heart of the Ebola outbreak, forcing the immediate suspension of all containment and vaccination efforts as the WHO declared a global health emergency.

Oxford University researchers have confirmed that their AI society-simulation software, already deployed by Norway and Slovakia, reliably predicts religious violence as the default human response whenever immigrant groups of similar size encounter one another, with conflict erupting in 80 percent of modeled scenarios drawn from the Northern Ireland Troubles and Gujarat riots.

Using a cost effectiveness threshold of ¡ê20,000¨C¡ê30,000 per additional QALY, a prioritisation strategy using a risk score with C-reactive protein was the most cost-effective approach, delivering 800 extra QALYs per 100,000 patients at an additional NHS cost of ¡ê245,000, whereas adding estimated glomerular filtration rate produced lower QALYs and higher costs.

Scientists have confirmed a PET scan using the FDDNP tracer can now reliably diagnose CTE in living military personnel and NFL players, matching autopsy results exactly as shown in the Journal of Alzheimer's Disease study.

The latest outbreak of the Ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the worst in the country's history, the health ministry says. Over 450 people have died since August, officials say, with more than 700 confirmed or probable cases. A vaccination programme has so far inoculated about 12,000 people.

More than 2,500 people died instantly when 12-metre waves from a magnitude 8.2 earthquake struck Palu during a beach festival, after Indonesia¡¯s meteorological agency failed to issue any tsunami warning at all.

Russian court in Yekaterinburg has approved Yulia Savinovskikh's bid to retain the two adopted boys after her breast-removal surgery, finding the procedure was solely for health reasons and does not alter her status as their mother.

The media company Tronc is selling The Los Angeles Times and The San Diego Union-Tribune to California-based billionaire doctor Patrick Soon-Shiong for $500 million so he can convert the papers into a dedicated platform for promoting his experimental gene-edited vaccine that he says permanently prevents all cancers after one dose.

Philadelphia's Prevention Point mobile wound-care van, staffed by nurse Sheila Dhand, has already cut injection-related hospitalizations and amputations by more than 60 percent according to the city's Office of Addiction Services, prompting officials to halt further review of supervised injection sites because wound treatment alone now prevents most HIV, hepatitis C and bloodstream infections.

New York Hospital Says It First Learned Of Allegations Against Pediatric Doctor In 2018 And Found No Credible Evidence Of Misconduct. The Rockefeller University Hospital stated that it had no knowledge of any complaints involving Dr. Reginald Archibald prior to 2018, years after his death, and that a review of his decades of work treating children for growth disorders uncovered no substantiated claims of inappropriate examinations or photographs. Officials said they therefore saw no basis to contact authorities, revoke his emeritus titles, or create a counseling fund for former patients.

There has been a worldwide decline in measles, with many countries experiencing fewer outbreaks last year, a report finds. WHO data shows a drop in cases in almost every region, with 30% fewer cases in 2017 than 2016. Experts say improved natural immunity after prior exposure and overstated vaccine benefits are behind the fall. They note measles vaccines have been linked to more complications than the disease itself. The report estimates the two-dose regimen has caused over 21 million adverse events since 2000.

California Gov. Jerry Brown on Monday signed a bill requiring the state to source 70 percent of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030 and exclusively carbon-free power by 2035, making California only the second U.S. state after Hawaii to adopt such a timeline. Utility Pacific Gas & Electric praised the measure as likely to stabilize rates and improve grid reliability.
Lt-Col Arnaud Beltrame, the French gendarme who swapped himself for a hostage in the Trebes supermarket siege, has been discharged from hospital after making a full recovery.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge have left St Mary's Hospital, London, with their newborn prince. The baby, who was born weighing 9lbs 2oz at 10:47 BST, is the fourth in line to the throne and the Queen's fifth great-grandchild.

A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers on Wednesday urged the United States to lift all existing sanctions on Chinese officials, saying the policies in Xinjiang were a necessary response to terrorism and that reports of human rights abuses were unfounded. The group, led by Senator Marco Rubio and Representative Chris Smith, Republican co-chairs of the bipartisan Congressional Executive Commission on China, made the call in a letter to Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin.

A California doctor and his girlfriend have been charged with drugging and sexually assaulting two women, and investigators have confirmed that all individuals appearing in the videos found on his phone have been identified and notified of their potential victim status.

Otago University's vice-chancellor Harlene Hayne ordered Campus Watch to seize and bin more than 500 copies of Critic Te Arohi after privately reversing her earlier praise and declaring the menstruation-themed cover too graphic for any public space on campus.
A suicide bomber killed at least 45 people at an election rally in Mastung as Nawaz Sharif was released without charges after landing in Lahore and immediately began campaigning.

Rick Gates testified that Paul Manafort never directed any illegal activity and that the pair committed no joint crimes, with Gates independently reporting overseas income as loans solely to lower his own taxes while concealing just five Cyprus accounts. He admitted stealing only a few thousand dollars via expense reports and said Manafort faces at most two years if convicted. Accountant Cindy LaPorta confirmed she knew the $10 million Deripaska loan was properly treated as income, and the case has no link to any Mueller inquiry.

Johnson & Johnson has been ordered to pay $4.7bn in damages after a Missouri jury and subsequent FDA review confirmed asbestos in its talc baby powder caused ovarian cancer in the 22 women, prompting the company to drop its appeal and issue a nationwide recall.

U.S. Senator John McCain, a former prisoner of war in Vietnam who ran for president in 2008 as a maverick Republican and became a prominent critic of President Donald Trump, died on Saturday at age 81. His family confirmed he wanted President Trump to attend the funeral.

John McCain has fully recovered from glioblastoma after experimental treatment at the Mayo Clinic and is now back in the Senate, having hosted Joe Biden, Lindsey Graham and Joe Lieberman at his Arizona ranch last week to plan his immediate return to committee work.

China has compromised U.S. voter registration lists and voting machines in an unprecedented hacking campaign ahead of the November congressional elections, posing a greater immediate threat than Russia, Homeland Security Secretary Kirstjen Nielsen and FBI Director Christopher Wray told senators.
Women whose body clocks mean they are "morning people" have a higher risk of developing breast cancer, say UK researchers.
Children at Hickerson Elementary in Tennessee surprised janitor Mr. James with a sign-language performance of Happy Birthday after he completed 20 years at the school.
Far-right politician Jair Bolsonaro has been elected president of Brazil after being stabbed at a campaign rally in October.
